title: Ποιμὴν καὶ πρόβατα
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 316. Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Ποιμὴν εἰσελάσας τὰ πρόβατα εἴς τινα δρυμῶνα, ὡς ἐθεάσατο δρῦν παμμεγέθη μεστὴν βαλάνων, ὑποστρώσας τὸ ἱμάτιον αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ ταύτην ἀνέβη καὶ τὸν καρπὸν κατέσειε.
sentences.tr: Poimēn eiselasas ta probata eis tina drymōna, hōs etheasato dryn pammegethē mestēn balanōn, hypostrōsas to himation autou epi tautēn anebē kai ton karpon kateseie.
sentences.l: A shepherd, having driven his sheep into a certain thicket, when he saw an enormous oak full of acorns, having spread his cloak underneath, climbed up on to the oak and shook the fruit down.
sentences.i: A shepherd drove his sheep into a thicket, and when he saw an enormous oak full of acorns, he spread his cloak on the ground beneath it, climbed the tree, and shook the crop down.
sentences.n: μεστός takes the genitive of what a thing is full of. ὑποστρώσας, 'having spread underneath', is the small act that makes the whole disaster possible. κατέσειε is imperfect: the shaking goes on above while the eating goes on below.

sentences.t: Τὰ δὲ πρόβατα ἐσθίοντα τὰς βαλάνους ἔλαθε καὶ τὰ ἱμάτια συγκαταφαγόντα.
sentences.tr: Ta de probata esthionta tas balanous elathe kai ta himatia synkataphagonta.
sentences.l: But the sheep, eating the acorns, escaped notice devouring the clothes along with them.
sentences.i: But the sheep, as they ate the acorns, ate up the clothes along with them and were not seen doing it.
sentences.n: λανθάνω once more with a supplementary participle: συγκαταφαγόντα carries the action, and ἔλαθε says only that it passed unnoticed — the same idiom as in fable 313's moral. ἔλαθε is singular with a neuter plural subject. The plural τὰ ἱμάτια after the singular τὸ ἱμάτιον above is what the page prints.

sentences.t: Ὁ δὲ ποιμὴν καταβάς, ὡς ἐθεάσατο τὸ γεγονός, εἶπεν· « Ὦ κάκιστα ζῷα, ὑμεῖς τοῖς λοιποῖς ἔρια εἰς ἐσθῆτας παρεχόμενα, ἐμοῦ τοῦ τρέφοντος καὶ τὸ ἱμάτιον ἀφείλεσθε. »
sentences.tr: Ho de poimēn katabas, hōs etheasato to gegonos, eipen· « Ō kakista zōia, hymeis tois loipois eria eis esthētas parechomena, emou tou trephontos kai to himation apheilesthe. »
sentences.l: And the shepherd, having come down, when he saw what had happened, said: « O most wicked creatures, you who furnish the rest with wool for clothing, from me, the one who feeds you, have taken away even my cloak. »
sentences.i: And the shepherd came down, saw what had happened, and said: « You vilest of beasts — you supply everyone else with wool for their clothing, and from me, who feed you, you have taken even the cloak off my back. »
sentences.n: ἀφαιρέομαι in the middle is 'take away from' and governs the genitive of the person robbed: ἐμοῦ τοῦ τρέφοντος, 'from me, the one who feeds you'. τὸ γεγονός, the perfect participle under the article, is 'what has happened'. παρεχόμενα is middle — they furnish the wool out of themselves — and neuter, agreeing with ζῷα although the address is second person; the Greek slides from address into description without repairing the person.

sentences.t: Οὕτω τῶν ἀνθρώπων πολλοὶ δι’ ἄγνοιαν τοὺς μηδὲν προσήκοντας εὐεργετοῦντες κατὰ τῶν οἰκείων φαῦλα ἐργάζονται.
sentences.tr: Houtō tōn anthrōpōn polloi di’ agnoian tous mēden prosēkontas euergetountes kata tōn oikeiōn phaula ergazontai.
sentences.l: Thus many among men, through ignorance, doing good to those who are nothing to them, work harm against their own.
sentences.i: Thus many among men, out of sheer ignorance, do kindnesses to people who are nothing to them and do their own people harm by it.
sentences.n: οἱ μηδὲν προσήκοντες, 'those belonging in nothing', are outsiders with no claim on one; οἱ οἰκεῖοι are one's own household and kin. κατά with the genitive is hostile, 'against'.
